requirements.text: The ESA sample(s) submitted for type approval shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark.
The ESA sample(s) submitted for type approval shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the type designation.
An approval mark as described in UN R10 paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every vehicle conforming to a type approved under UN R10.

An approval mark as described in UN R10 paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under UN R10, except where the electrical/electronic system is built into a vehicle approved as a unit, in which case no marking is required.
An international approval mark shall be affixed on each vehicle conforming to the type approved under UN R10 in a conspicuous and easily accessible place specified on the approval communication form.

The international approval mark affixed on each vehicle conforming to the type approved under UN R10 shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.

The international approval mark affixed on each vehicle conforming to the type approved under UN R10 shall comprise the number of the Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number to the right of the circle containing the letter "E".

The vehicle and its electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s), including the ACPE system, shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of UN R10.
The vehicle fitted with the ACPE system shall be tested for radiated emissions.
The vehicle fitted with the ACPE system shall be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances.
The ACPE ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated emissions.
The ACPE ESA(s) shall be tested for conducted emissions.
The ACPE ESA(s) shall be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances.
The ACPE ESA(s) shall be tested for immunity to conducted disturbances.
The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the vehicle representative of its type shall be measured using the method described in Annex 4.

Where measured using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle broadband electromagnetic radiation shall not exceed 32 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band.

Where measured using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle broadband electromagnetic radiation shall not exceed the limit of 32 to 43 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequency.
The vehicle broadband radiated emission limit shall remain constant at 43 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band, as shown in Appendix 2.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle broadband radiated emission limit shall be 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle broadband radiated emission limit shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 3.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle broadband radiated emission limit shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
The measured broadband radiated emission values of the vehicle representative of its type, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the vehicle representative of its type shall be measured using the method described in Annex 5.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle narrowband radiated emission limit shall be 28 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 230 MHz frequency band.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle narrowband radiated emission limit shall be 35 dB microvolts/m in the 230 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle narrowband radiated emission limit shall be 38 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 230 MHz frequency band.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle narrowband radiated emission limit shall be 45 dB microvolts/m in the 230 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
The measured narrowband radiated emission values of the vehicle representative of its type, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limit.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the vehicle representative of its type, including the ACPE system, shall be tested by the method described in Annex 6.

Where vehicle immunity is tested using the method described in Annex 6 in accordance with ISO 11451-2, the vehicle with the ACPE system shall be subjected to a field strength of 30 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 25 volts/m over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

Where vehicle immunity is tested using the method described in Annex 6 in accordance with ISO 11451-2, the vehicle with the ACPE system shall be subjected to a field strength of 10 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 8 volts/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.

Where vehicle immunity is tested using the method described in Annex 6 in accordance with ISO 11451-4 BCI, the vehicle with the ACPE system shall be subjected to a current of 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

The vehicle representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions", according to paragraph 2.1. of Annex 6, including the ACPE system, during the immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 6.
The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ACPE ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.

Where measured using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband radiated emissions of the ACPE ESA shall not exceed 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, the limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.

Where measured using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband radiated emissions of the ACPE ESA shall not exceed 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, the limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.
Where measured using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband radiated emissions of the ACPE ESA shall not exceed a constant limit of 63 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
The broadband emission values measured on the ACPE ESA representative of its type, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ACPE ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.

Where measured using the method described in Annex 8, the narrowband radiated emissions of the ACPE ESA shall not exceed 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, the limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.

Where measured using the method described in Annex 8, the narrowband radiated emissions of the ACPE ESA shall not exceed 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, the limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.
Where measured using the method described in Annex 8, the narrowband radiated emissions of the ACPE ESA shall not exceed a constant limit of 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
The narrowband emission values measured on the ACPE ESA representative of its type, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances on 12/24 V supply lines of the ACPE ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
The positive transient conducted emission pulse amplitude of the ACPE ESA shall not exceed +75 V for vehicles with 12 V systems.
The positive transient conducted emission pulse amplitude of the ACPE ESA shall not exceed +150 V for vehicles with 24 V systems.
The negative transient conducted emission pulse amplitude of the ACPE ESA shall not exceed -100 V for vehicles with 12 V systems.
The negative transient conducted emission pulse amplitude of the ACPE ESA shall not exceed -450 V for vehicles with 24 V systems.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ACPE ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.
The ACPE ESA shall withstand a stripline test level of 60 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.
The ACPE ESA shall withstand a TEM cell test level of 75 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 200 MHz frequency range.
The ACPE ESA shall withstand a BCI test level of 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.
The ACPE ESA shall withstand an ALSE test level of 30 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency range.
The ACPE ESA shall withstand an ALSE test level of 10 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range.
The ACPE ESA shall withstand a reverberation chamber test level of 21 V/m in over 90 per cent of the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range.
The ACPE ESA shall withstand a reverberation chamber test level of 7 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range.
The ACPE ESA shall withstand a minimum stripline test level of 50 V/m over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.
The ACPE ESA shall withstand a minimum TEM cell test level of 62,5 V/m over the whole 20 to 200 MHz frequency range.
The ACPE ESA shall withstand a minimum BCI test level of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.
The ACPE ESA shall withstand a minimum ALSE test level of 25 V/m over the whole 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency range.
The ACPE ESA shall withstand a minimum ALSE test level of 8 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range.
The ACPE ESA shall withstand a minimum reverberation chamber test level of 18 V/m over the whole LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range.
The ACPE ESA shall withstand a minimum reverberation chamber test level of 6 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range.
The ACPE ESA shall show no degradation of performance of immunity related functions during the radiated immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 9.

The immunity of the ACPE ESA to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested according to ISO 16750-2 for starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.

For installation in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12V/24V starter motor, the ACPE ESA shall withstand the starting profile at immunity test level II (12 V and 24 V systems) for 10 pulses with functional status B for immunity related functions where the ESA shall be operational during engine start phases, and C for other ESA, as defined in ISO 16750-1.
For the starting profile, functions of the ACPE ESA not related to immunity related functions shall achieve functional status D.
The ACPE ESA shall withstand test pulse 1 at -75 V (12 V system) or -450 V (24 V system) for 500 pulses with FPSC III.

The ACPE ESA shall withstand test pulse 2a at +37 V (12 V and 24 V systems) for 500 pulses with FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

The ACPE ESA shall withstand test pulse 2b at +10 V (12 V system) or +20 V (24 V system) for 10 pulses with FPSC II for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

The ACPE ESA shall withstand test pulse 3a at -112 V (12 V system) or -150 V (24 V system) for 1 h with FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

The ACPE ESA shall withstand test pulse 3b at +75 V (12 V system) or +150 V (24 V system) for 1 h with FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

Where measured by the method of Annex 4 at a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the broadband emission of the vehicle fitted with the ACPE system shall not exceed 32 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band.

Where measured by the method of Annex 4 at a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the broadband emission of the vehicle fitted with the ACPE system shall not exceed 32 to 43 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, the limit increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 2.

Where measured by the method of Annex 4 at a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the broadband emission of the vehicle fitted with the ACPE system shall not exceed 43 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.

Where measured by the method of Annex 4 at a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the broadband emission of the vehicle fitted with the ACPE system shall be below 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band.

Where measured by the method of Annex 4 at a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the broadband emission of the vehicle fitted with the ACPE system shall be below 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, the limit increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 3.

Where measured by the method of Annex 4 at a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the broadband emission of the vehicle fitted with the ACPE system shall be below 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the vehicle equipped with the ACPE system representative of its type shall be tested by the method described in Annex 6.

For tests made using the method described in Annex 6, the vehicle shall be immune at a field strength of 30 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 25 volts/m over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

For tests made using the method described in Annex 6, the vehicle shall be immune at a field strength of 10 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 8 volts/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.

For tests made using the method described in Annex 6 with the ISO 11451-4 BCI method, the vehicle shall be immune at a current of 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

During the immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 6, there shall be no degradation of performance of the "immunity related functions" of the vehicle, including the ACPE system, according to paragraph 2.2. of Annex 6.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ACPE ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.

For measurements made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband radiated emissions of the ACPE ESA shall not exceed 62 to 52 dBµV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz.

For measurements made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband radiated emissions of the ACPE ESA shall not exceed 52 to 63 dBµV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6.
For measurements made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband radiated emissions of the ACPE ESA shall not exceed a constant 63 dBµV/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
The measured broadband emission values of the ACPE ESA representative of its type, expressed in dBµV/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

Where the ACPE ESA is added or substituted without approval pursuant to UN R10 and testing is considered necessary, the new or revised part shall conform to the relevant requirements of paragraph 6 and, if applicable, paragraph 7, or shall be shown in a comparative test not to be likely to adversely affect the conformity of the vehicle type.
The vehicle broadband radiated emission measured at an antenna-vehicle separation of 10 m shall not exceed the limit E = 32 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 30-75 MHz.

The vehicle broadband radiated emission measured at an antenna-vehicle separation of 10 m shall not exceed the limit E = 32 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m (F in MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 75-400 MHz.
The vehicle broadband radiated emission measured at an antenna-vehicle separation of 10 m shall not exceed the limit E = 43 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 400-1,000 MHz.
The vehicle broadband radiated emission measured at an antenna-vehicle separation of 3 m shall not exceed the limit E = 42 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 30-75 MHz.

The vehicle broadband radiated emission measured at an antenna-vehicle separation of 3 m shall not exceed the limit E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m (F in MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 75-400 MHz.
The vehicle broadband radiated emission measured at an antenna-vehicle separation of 3 m shall not exceed the limit E = 53 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the frequency range 400-1,000 MHz.
The vehicle narrowband radiated emissions, measured at an antenna-vehicle separation of 10 m with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the limit E = 28 dBµV/m for the frequency range 30-230 MHz.
The vehicle narrowband radiated emissions, measured at an antenna-vehicle separation of 10 m with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the limit E = 35 dBµV/m for the frequency range 230-1,000 MHz.
The vehicle narrowband radiated emissions, measured at an antenna-vehicle separation of 3 m with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the limit E = 38 dBµV/m for the frequency range 30-230 MHz.
The vehicle narrowband radiated emissions, measured at an antenna-vehicle separation of 3 m with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the limit E = 45 dBµV/m for the frequency range 230-1,000 MHz.
The ESA broadband radiated emissions, for a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the limit E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m for the frequency range 30-75 MHz.
The ESA broadband radiated emissions, for a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the limit E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m for the frequency range 75-400 MHz.
The ESA broadband radiated emissions, for a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the limit E = 63 dBµV/m for the frequency range 400-1,000 MHz.
The ESA narrowband radiated emissions, for a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the limit E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m for the frequency range 30-75 MHz.
The ESA narrowband radiated emissions, for a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the limit E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m for the frequency range 75-400 MHz.
The ESA narrowband radiated emissions, for a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the limit E = 53 dBµV/m for the frequency range 400-1,000 MHz.

The vehicle fitted with the ACPE system shall be tested for broadband emissions generated by its electrical or electronic systems (e.g. ignition system or electric motors) according to CISPR 12, if not otherwise stated in Annex 4.
The engine of the vehicle in configuration other than "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" shall be in operation according to CISPR 12 during the broadband emission test.

Where the operating mode defined in CISPR 12 (i.e. 40 km/h) does not activate all traction motors or auxiliary battery charging engines of a vehicle with an electric propulsion motor or hybrid propulsion system, the vehicle shall be operated in an alternative, steady state operating mode agreed between the Technical Service and vehicle manufacturer.

All vehicle equipment capable of generating broadband emissions which can be switched on permanently by the driver or passenger, including the ACPE system, should be in operation in maximum load during the test of the vehicle in configuration other than "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid".
The vehicle, where a charging mode is available, shall be tested in the "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" configuration as defined in the flowchart of Figure 1 of Annex 4.
The vehicle in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" shall be immobilized, with the engine(s) (ICE and / or electrical engine) OFF and in charging mode during the test.
All other equipment which can be switched ON by the driver or passengers shall be OFF during the test of the vehicle in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid".

The vehicle shall meet the radiated emission limits throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or an outdoor test site (OTS).
Where peak detectors are used, the vehicle shall meet the quasi-peak limits given in paragraphs 6.2. and 7.2. with a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 applied.
During the narrowband electromagnetic emission test, the vehicle ignition switch shall be switched on.
During the narrowband electromagnetic emission test, the vehicle engine shall not be operating.
During the narrowband electromagnetic emission test, the vehicle's electronic systems, including the ACPE system, shall all be in normal operating mode with the vehicle stationary.

During the narrowband electromagnetic emission test, all equipment which can be switched on permanently by the driver or passenger with internal oscillators > 9 kHz or repetitive signals should be in normal operation.

The vehicle narrowband electromagnetic radiated emissions shall comply with the limits throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or an outdoor test site (OTS).
The vehicle shall demonstrate the immunity of its electronic systems, including the ACPE system, when subjected to electromagnetic fields as described in Annex 6.
The vehicle shall be tested according to ISO 11451-2 in an ALSE with front irradiation, unless otherwise stated in Annex 6.
The vehicle immunity tests shall be performed with the levels defined in paragraph 6.4.2.1. of UN R10.

Where the vehicle immunity test is performed in an outdoor test site, the vehicle shall be tested according to ISO 11451-2 in an OTS with front irradiation at the levels defined in paragraph 6.4.2.1. of UN R10.
The vehicle shall be in an unladen condition, except for necessary test equipment, during the immunity test.
During the immunity test, the engine shall normally turn the driving wheels at a steady speed of 50 km/h if there is no technical reason due to the vehicle to define a different condition.
Other vehicle systems that can affect immunity related functions, such as the ACPE system, shall be tested in a way agreed between the manufacturer and the Technical Service.
In the 50 km/h mode immunity test, the vehicle speed shall be 50 km/h ±20 per cent with the vehicle driving the rollers.
In the 50 km/h mode immunity test, the vehicle shall not show a speed variation greater than ±10 per cent of the nominal speed.

For vehicles with an automatic gearbox, the vehicle shall not show a change of gear ratio inducing a speed variation greater than ±10 per cent of the nominal speed during the 50 km/h mode immunity test.

If the vehicle is equipped with a cruise control system, it shall be used to maintain the required constant vehicle speed and shall be maintained without any deactivation during the 50 km/h mode immunity test.
In the 50 km/h mode immunity test, the instrument cluster shall operate in normal mode and shall not show an unexpected warning.
In the 50 km/h mode immunity test, with the brake pedal not depressed, there shall be no unexpected activation of the brake and no unexpected activation of the stop lights.
All equipment which can be switched on permanently by the driver or passenger should be in normal operation during the immunity test.
All other systems which affect the driver's control of the vehicle, including the ACPE system, shall be on as in normal operation of the vehicle during the immunity test.

The vehicle shall not set in motion during the immunity test in the "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" configuration, with the REESS in charging mode and the REESS state of charge kept between 20 per cent and 80 per cent of the maximum SOC.
The parking brake shall not be unexpectedly released during the immunity test in the "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" configuration.
For vehicles with automatic transmission, the parking position shall not be lost during the immunity test in the "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" configuration.

For AC charging during the immunity test in "REESS charging mode", if the current consumption can be adjusted, the charging current shall be set to at least 20 per cent of its maximum rated charging/input current value.

For DC charging during the immunity test in "REESS charging mode", if the current consumption can be adjusted, the charging current shall be set to at least 20 per cent of its maximum value or to a minimum of 16 A, unless another value is agreed with the Type Approval Authorities.
The vehicle fitted with the ACPE system shall be exposed to electromagnetic radiation in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges in vertical polarization.

The test signal modulation applied to the vehicle fitted with the ACPE system shall be AM (amplitude modulation), with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth, in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and vehicle manufacturer.

The test signal modulation applied to the vehicle fitted with the ACPE system shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs, in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and vehicle manufacturer.

The test signal modulation applied to the vehicle fitted with the ACPE system shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs, in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and vehicle manufacturer.
The ACPE ESA under broadband emission test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.

The radiated emissions of the ACPE electronic sub-assembly shall not exceed the limits throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).

The radiated emissions of the ACPE electronic sub-assembly shall comply with the limits given in paragraphs 6.5. and 7.10. for quasi-peak detectors, with a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 applied where peak detectors are used.
The ACPE electronic sub-assembly's narrowband electromagnetic emissions shall be tested according to CISPR 25, unless otherwise stated in Annex 8 of UN R10.
The ACPE electronic sub-assembly shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load, during the narrowband electromagnetic emission tests.

The ACPE electronic sub-assembly's narrowband electromagnetic emissions shall not exceed the limits given in paragraph 6.6.2.1. of UN R10 throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz, measured in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).

The ESA shall comply with the immunity requirements of any combination, at the manufacturer's discretion, of the absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2, TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3, bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4, stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5 and reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11, provided that the results cover the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of Annex 9.
The frequency range and general test conditions for the ESA immunity tests shall be based on ISO 11452-1.
The ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition during the immunity tests.
The ESA under test shall be arranged as defined in Annex 9 unless individual test methods dictate otherwise.
The ESA shall be subjected to immunity measurements in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.

The ESA immunity test signal modulation shall be AM (amplitude modulation), with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth, in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The ESA immunity test signal modulation shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs, in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The ESA immunity test signal modulation shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs, in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
The wiring harness connecting the components of the ACPE ESA shall be tested for immunity by stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5.
Where the reverberation chamber test is used, the ACPE ESA shall be tested for immunity according to ISO 11452-11.
Unless otherwise specified, the reverberation chamber testing of the ACPE ESA shall be carried out using a test setup with ground plane.
The ACPE ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply.
The ACPE ESA shall limit conducted transients from the ESA to the vehicle power supply.

The ACPE ESA shall be immune to test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

For ACPE ESAs not exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles without 12V/24V starter motor, the ESA shall be immune to the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 applied to the supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ACPE ESA on 12/24 V supply lines and on other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines shall be measured according to ISO 7637-2.

The vehicle with the ACPE system, in the configuration "REESS in charging mode coupled to the power grid", shall meet the electrical fast transient/burst immunity requirements when tested in accordance with IEC 61000-4-4 at the severity levels given in paragraph 7.8.2.1.

The vehicle with the ACPE system, in the configuration "REESS in charging mode coupled to the power grid", shall meet the immunity requirements when the electrical fast transient/burst (EFT/B) is applied on the AC/DC power lines in common modes using a CDN as described in Figures 1a to 1d of Appendix 1 to Annex 15.

The vehicle electronic systems shall be immune to surges conducted along the AC and DC power lines of the vehicle as described in Annex 16, with the test performed according to IEC 61000-4-5, Clause 4.2 for lightning transients unless otherwise stated in Annex 16.

The vehicle shall be tested for surge immunity in the "REESS in charging mode coupled to the power grid" configuration, where this charging mode is available on the vehicle, as defined in the flowchart of Figure 1.

The vehicle shall not set itself in motion during the surge immunity test in REESS charging mode, with the REESS in charging mode and the traction battery state of charge kept between 20 per cent and 80 per cent of the maximum SOC.
The vehicle shall not unexpectedly release the parking brake during the surge immunity test in REESS charging mode.
For automatic transmission vehicles, the vehicle shall not lose the parking position during the surge immunity test in REESS charging mode.

Every vehicle conforming to a vehicle type approved under UN R175 shall bear an international approval mark conforming to the model described in Annex 2, affixed conspicuously and in a readily accessible place specified on the approval form.
The international approval mark shall consist of a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
The international approval mark shall include the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number, to the right of the circle surrounding the letter "E".

Where the vehicle conforms to a vehicle type approved under one or more other Regulations annexed to the Agreement in the country which has granted approval under this Regulation and the circle surrounding the letter "E" is not repeated, the Regulation and approval numbers and the additional symbols shall be placed in vertical columns to the right of the circle surrounding the letter "E".
The approval mark shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The approval mark shall be placed close to or on the vehicle data plate.

The ACPE performance requirements shall be met by a vehicle with no trailer coupled, with a mass between maximum mass and mass in running order, and whose powertrain management system is properly operational.

The ACPE shall be able to limit unintended acceleration of the vehicle when an accelerator control misapplication by the driver has been detected at least when an obstacle exists in front of the vehicle when the driving direction is selected to be forward.

The ACPE shall be able to limit unintended acceleration of the vehicle when an accelerator control misapplication by the driver has been detected at least when an obstacle exists behind the vehicle when the driving direction is selected to be rearwards.

The ACPE shall regard as an accelerator control misapplication an accelerator control application having a velocity of at least 400 per cent per second over a travel distance of at least 70 per cent of the total travel distance of the accelerator control and reaching a maximum position of the accelerator control of at least 90 per cent with that velocity.
The ACPE shall control acceleration when the vehicle is accelerated from standstill.
If the ACPE is not ready to perform an intervention 6 seconds after the initiation of the vehicle powertrain, information of this status shall be indicated to the driver.
The information that the ACPE is not ready to perform an intervention shall exist until the system has been successfully initialised.

The ACPE shall limit vehicle acceleration in order to prevent or mitigate a collision with an obstacle located between 1.0 m and 1.5 m in front of or behind the vehicle, in the vehicle path, at the time the accelerator control is applied, provided the road is flat, horizontal and dry affording good adhesion, the weather conditions do not affect the performance of the vehicle, the tyres are in an appropriate state and properly inflated, the brakes if intended to be used are properly operational, there is no severe uneven load distribution, no trailer is coupled and the vehicle mass is between maximum mass and mass in running order, the powertrain management system is properly operational, the ambient illumination is at least 1000 Lux with no extreme blinding of the sensors, the target is not extreme with regard to Radar Cross Section or shape/silhouette, there are no significant weather conditions affecting sensing, there are no overhead obstructions close to the vehicle, the obstacle is stationary, unobstructed and clearly separated from other objects in the driving direction, the lateral offset between the centrelines of the obstacle and the vehicle is not more than 0.2 m, the direction of travel is straight with no curve and the vehicle is not turning at an intersection, and the obstacle is a vehicle of category M1 or a wall like structure with a width of at least 2.0 m and a height of at least 1.0 m.
When conditions deviate from those listed for the ACPE performance requirement, the ACPE shall not deactivate or unreasonably switch the control strategy, as demonstrated in accordance with Annex 3.

In the case that a collision is not prevented, the collision speed shall be no greater than 8 km/h higher than the vehicle speed at the point where the accelerator control misapplication triggering conditions are met.

In the case that a collision is not prevented, the collision speed shall not be greater than 70% of the speed the vehicle would have had in the same position and under the same circumstances but without any ACPE intervention.

For vehicles that do not exceed 8 km/h without ACPE in the test scenarios but for which a speed reduction of 30 per cent cannot be achieved due to a low engine power to test mass ratio, the speed reduction achieved by the ACPE shall be at least 15 per cent.
During any intervention, the vehicle acceleration shall continue to be limited by the ACPE.
The ACPE intervention shall only be ended when the obstacle is no longer detected or the driver has interrupted the function.
The effectiveness of the ACPE shall not be adversely affected by magnetic or electrical fields.
The ACPE shall fulfil the technical requirements of the 06 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 10.
The ACPE shall meet the requirements of Annex 3 concerning the safety aspects of electronic control systems.
The ACPE shall inform the driver of its intervention in accordance with paragraph 5.4.2.
The ACPE shall provide a means for the driver to interrupt its intervention.
The interruption of the ACPE intervention shall be started by any intentional action which indicates that the driver has recognised the situation.
In the case of interruption of the ACPE intervention by maintaining the accelerator control application, there shall be no rapid increase of acceleration.
The ACPE shall meet the performance requirements when tested according to the test procedure described in section 6.

Where the vehicle is equipped with a means to manually deactivate the ACPE, the ACPE shall be automatically reinstated at the initiation of any new engine start (or run cycle, as relevant), except when the new engine start (or run cycle) is performed automatically, e.g. by the operation of a stop/start system.
Where the ACPE is manually deactivated, a deactivation warning shall be given at least at the time of deactivation.
A failure warning shall be given to the driver when there is a failure in the ACPE that prevents the requirements of UN R175 being met.
The ACPE failure warning shall be as specified in paragraph 5.4.3.
There shall not be an appreciable time interval between each ACPE self-check.

In the case of an electrically detectable failure, there shall not be a delay in illuminating the ACPE warning signal, except that if the vehicle speed is greater than 10 km/h at the time the failure is detected the warning signal may be suppressed until the next time the vehicle speed is below 10 km/h.

A failure warning shall be given to the driver in the case of a detected non-electrical ACPE failure condition (e.g. sensor blindness or sensor misalignment), unless a deactivation warning is given as per paragraph 5.2.3.1.3.
The ACPE optical warning signals shall be visible even by daylight.
The satisfactory condition of the ACPE optical warning signals shall be easily verifiable by the driver from the driver's seat.

Each ACPE optical warning signal not shown in a common space shall be activated either when the engine start (or run, as relevant) switch is turned to the "on" (run) position or when the switch is in a position between the "on" (run) and "start" position designated by the manufacturer as a check position (initial system (power-on)).
The ACPE intervention warning shall be given by an optical signal.

In addition to the optical signal, a haptic or acoustic ACPE intervention signal shall be provided to the driver, unless such a signal is already being provided by another vehicle system comprising an object detection capability (e.g. parking distance warning).
The ACPE failure warning shall be given by a constant yellow optical signal.
The ACPE shall allow its correct operational status to be confirmed at a Periodic Technical Inspection by a visible observation of the failure warning signal status.

Following a "power-ON" and any bulb check, the ACPE failure warning signal shall remain illuminated if any failure was present at the end of the previous engine start (or run, as relevant) cycle, unless this failure is detected to be no longer present.

The operation of the ACPE failure warning signal shall be protected against simple unauthorised modification, unless a secondary means of checking the correct operational status of the ACPE is available.

Where, at the request of the manufacturer and with the agreement of the Technical Service, tests are conducted under deviating test conditions (suboptimal conditions, e.g. on a not dry surface or below the specified minimum ambient temperature), the ACPE system shall still meet the performance requirements.
The ACPE shall meet the performance requirements with the vehicle at the minimum mass (mass in running order with an additional mass of maximum 125 kg).
The ACPE shall meet the performance requirements at any other vehicle mass up to the technically permissible maximum laden mass as defined by the manufacturer, where such a test mass is selected.
The ACPE shall meet the accelerator control misapplication test requirements both with and without an expected ACPE intervention.
The ACPE shall meet the accelerator control misapplication test requirements in both a forward and a rearward direction.

The ACPE shall meet the accelerator control misapplication test requirements at least with the vehicle situated 1.0 m (+0.1 m tolerance) and 1.5 m (-0.1 m tolerance) from the target position at the start of the test.
The dimension a of the approval mark affixed to the vehicle shall be at least 8 mm.
The ACPE system shall respect, under non-fault and fault conditions, all the appropriate performance requirements specified in UN R175.
The ACPE system shall be designed to operate in such a way that it does not induce safety critical risks.
The ACPE system shall be designed to operate, under non-fault and fault conditions, in such a way that it does not induce safety critical risks.
The ACPE system shall respect, under non-fault and fault conditions, all the appropriate performance requirements specified elsewhere in UN R175.

Each unit of the ACPE system shall be clearly and unambiguously identifiable (e.g. by marking for hardware and marking or software output for software content) to provide corresponding hardware and documentation association.

Where ACPE functions are combined within a single unit or within a single computer but shown in multiple blocks in the block diagram, only a single hardware identification marking shall be used for that unit.
The identification of an ACPE system unit shall define the hardware and software version.
The identification of an ACPE system unit shall be changed where the software changes such as to alter the function of the unit as far as UN R175 is concerned.
In case of a failure of the ACPE system, the driver shall be warned, for example by warning signal or message display.

Where the ACPE system is not deactivated by the driver (e.g. by turning the ignition (run) switch to "off" or by switching off the function with a special switch), the failure warning shall be present as long as the fault condition persists.

If the chosen fault provision of the ACPE system selects the removal of the Higher Level Function, all the corresponding output control signals associated with this function shall be inhibited in such a manner as to limit the transition disturbance.

The ACPE system shall not prejudice the safe operation of the vehicle when its performance is affected by environmental conditions, e.g. climatic, temperature, dust ingress, water ingress, ice packing.
The ACPE system shall perform the functions declared by the manufacturer under non-fault conditions, including scenarios whereby a declared function is overridden.

The reaction of the ACPE system under the influence of a failure in any individual unit shall correspond with the documented summary of the failure analysis, to a level of overall effect such that the safety concept and execution are confirmed as being adequate.
